comparisons.title: Reference passages versus our complete organ registration
Our dry pipes: harmonic distribution and physical-flue bandwidth
Empires Will Fall at 1:48 versus our approximate pitch-matched chord

findings: Our current registration is substantially darker and narrower than the selected reference passages. Useful candidate organ/keyboard windows are Light of the Imperium 0:28–0:40 and Empires Will Fall 1:46–1:58; attribution from spectra alone remains uncertain.

The approximate pitch-matched probe uses G♯3/B3/D♯4 and the existing seven-rank registration. The reference window has 16.36% of its power at 2–12 kHz, versus 1.00% for our hall probe. Centroids are 1212 Hz and 387 Hz. These are mixed-reference versus organ measurements, not isolated-stop error scores.

The hall probe has a side/mid energy ratio of −21.5 dB, versus −3.4 dB in the reference window. The original Iron Choir registration with pedal is narrower still (−30.5 dB). Current spatial treatment contributes little width.

The next useful experiment is brighter reed/mixture voicing, deliberate rank placement and stronger spatial treatment, followed by controlled drive/rhythmic processing. The physical flue is a useful foundation and wind-response experiment; these recordings do not establish a need for a more complex physical solver.
